policy_title: Stop offshore tax avoidance by care home providers
stated: Reform UK will stop offshore tax avoidance by care home providers, specifically targeting larger providers avoiding tax on profits through complex offshore property company structures and high interest shareholder loans.

source.quote: Stop the Offshore Taxpayer Rip Off Some larger care home providers are avoiding tax on hundreds of millions of profits through complex offshore property company structures and high interest shareholder loans. This has to end.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets the financial structures of care home providers — the primary delivery mechanism for social care in later life — so stopping profit extraction through offshore vehicles and shareholder loans bears non-negligibly on the sustainability, funding, and quality of that care sector.

Closing offshore property-company structures and high-interest shareholder loan arrangements used by care home providers would increase UK tax receipts, directly improving the funded-vs-borrowed balance and debt-path sustainability.

These offshore avoidance structures disproportionately benefit wealthy investors and private-equity owners of care homes; closing them narrows the effective tax advantage accruing to the top, reducing wealth inequality through the distributional incidence of enforcement.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: a fiscal gain (O12) and a distributional gain (O14). O8 (social care) is considered but does not clear the bar — the policy does not change care funding, access or quality directly; providers meeting legal tax obligations is compliance, not a new cost burden that would plausibly reduce care capacity. O11 is not triggered as this is corporate not household tax. Other fundamentals are too remote.
